lessons.sourceTitleEnglish: The Guide Moves the Bus Up: Settle the Finca Order
lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Recount what the group ordered and paid, count items fast, and settle the bill before the bus leaves.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: You are the group's organizer, and the AI is Marleny, the cook at a coffee-farm breakfast near Salento: recount what the group ordered and who paid using the preterite (pedimos, pagaron), count what's still owed with faltan + numbers, and settle the bill before the bus leaves.
lessons.sourceGrammarFocusEnglish: Preterite narration; numbers under pressure (pedimos siete arepas, cuatro pagaron ya, faltan tres cafés)

sourceWordsEnglish.en: the scrambled eggs with tomato and onion
We ordered 7 arepas with cheese and 9 small black coffees.
Doña Marleny, 4 have already paid in cash.
There are still 3 black coffees and 2 aguapanelas to pay for.
Andrés said the minibus leaves in 10 minutes.
Guys, who ordered the scrambled eggs with tomato and onion?
Could you confirm how much of the balance is left, please?
Can I pay you by bank transfer or only in cash?
I'll pay what's left and sort it out with them later.

sourcePassageEnglish: At 7:30, Emma's group finished breakfast at a coffee farm near Salento.
Suddenly, the guide Andrés announced that they moved the departure up to 7:45 because of a landslide on the road.
Emma, the organizer, went to the kitchen and told the cook: Andrés said the minibus leaves in 10 minutes.
Doña Marleny opened the notebook where she wrote down the group's orders that morning.
Emma: We ordered 7 arepas with cheese and 9 small black coffees.
Marleny: Yes, and also 2 aguapanelas for Priya's kids.
Emma: Doña Marleny, 4 have already paid in cash.
Marleny: Okay, but I also served 2 calentados that nobody wrote down in the notebook.
Emma asked her companions: Guys, who ordered the scrambled eggs with tomato and onion?
Tom and Priya raised their hands, and Tom admitted that he also ate a calentado with farmer's cheese.
Marleny added it up quickly with her pencil and said: There are still 3 black coffees and 2 aguapanelas to pay for.
Emma: Could you confirm how much of the balance is left, please?
Marleny: The outstanding balance is 64 thousand pesos, with the scrambled eggs and the 2 calentados.
Emma only had large 100 thousand-peso bills, and Marleny didn't have change so early.
Emma: Can I pay you by bank transfer or only in cash?
Marleny answered that she does accept transfers through Nequi and showed her the number stuck on the wall.
Emma told her: I'll pay what's left and sort it out with them later.
Emma made the transfer of 64 thousand pesos, showed her the proof of payment, and ran to the minibus just in time.

sourceVerbsEnglish.meaningEnglish: to be missing, to be still owed

lessons.objectiveFrenchCourseEnglish: Recount a Québec farm café group order and settle a confirmed balance before a minibus leaves.

lessons.teachingNotesEnglish: In this fictional Québec farm café, recount the group order and paid items, ask for the displayed balance, and confirm the payment method before paying. Menu, payment options and departure time are details of this scene, not regional rules.

passage.titleFrench: Régler la commande avant le départ
english: At a farm café near Québec City, Emma’s group finishes breakfast before a guided outing.
The guide announces that the minibus must leave ten minutes earlier because the route has changed.
Emma asks the café worker for the order notebook so they can settle the bill.
The notebook lists toast with jam, black coffees, oatmeal, eggs and apple juice.
Emma says: We ordered seven toasts and nine small black coffees.
The worker confirms the order and points out two juices ordered for children.
Emma checks the receipts: Four people have already paid in cash.
The worker finds two bowls of oatmeal that were not marked as paid.
Emma asks her companions: Who ordered the scrambled eggs?
Two people answer, and one remembers an extra serving of local cheese.
The worker recounts the unpaid items with Emma, one by one.
Emma says: There are still three coffees and two juices to pay for.
She asks: Could you confirm the remaining balance, please?
The worker states the total and shows the list before Emma agrees.
Emma has only large bills and asks whether a bank transfer is possible.
The worker points to the accepted payment methods displayed at the register.
Emma pays the confirmed balance and keeps the proof of payment.
She tells the group she will settle their shares later, and they leave for the minibus.
french: Dans un café de ferme près de Québec, le groupe d’Emma termine son petit-déjeuner avant une sortie guidée.
Le guide annonce que le minibus doit partir dix minutes plus tôt, car l’itinéraire a changé.
Emma demande le carnet de commandes à la personne au comptoir pour régler l’addition.
Le carnet mentionne des tartines à la confiture, des cafés noirs, du gruau, des œufs et du jus de pomme.
Emma dit : « Nous avons commandé sept tartines et neuf petits cafés noirs. »
La personne confirme la commande et signale deux jus commandés pour les enfants.
Emma vérifie les reçus : « Quatre personnes ont déjà payé en espèces. »
La personne repère deux bols de gruau qui ne sont pas indiqués comme payés.
Emma demande à ses compagnons : « Qui a commandé les œufs brouillés ? »
Deux personnes répondent, et l’une se rappelle une portion supplémentaire de fromage local.
La personne reprend les articles non payés avec Emma, un par un.
Emma dit : « Il reste trois cafés et deux jus à payer. »
Elle demande : « Pourriez-vous confirmer le solde à payer, s’il vous plaît ? »
La personne annonce le total et montre la liste avant qu’Emma accepte.
Emma n’a que de gros billets et demande si un virement est possible.
La personne lui montre les moyens de paiement affichés à la caisse.
Emma règle le solde confirmé et garde la preuve de paiement.
Elle dit au groupe qu’elle répartira les frais plus tard, puis ils rejoignent le minibus.

lessons.sourceTitleEnglish: Decline the Offer to Scrape the Almonds Off
lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Refuse a well-meant but unsafe offer for an allergic friend and ask for a safe option or none at all.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: You are with your friend Kenji, who has a tree-nut allergy, and the AI is Jordi, a server at a granja in Gràcia: thank him warmly but turn down his offer with negative commands like no la raspes and no recomiendo que + subjunctive, then ask for a safe option or nothing at all.
lessons.sourceGrammarFocusEnglish: Negative commands; subjunctive after no recomiendo que (no lo raspes, por favor; no recomiendo que Kenji lo pruebe)

sourceWordsEnglish.en: the hot chocolate with whipped cream
Thanks, Jordi, but please don't scrape it.
I really appreciate it, honestly, you're very kind.
He has a severe tree-nut allergy.
I don't recommend Kenji try it, even if you remove the almonds.
Kenji, don't eat it; there are bits left in the dough.
Don't push it, Kenji; it's not worth the risk.
Do you have anything packaged, with the allergen label?
If there's no safe option, he'd rather not eat anything.

sourcePassageEnglish: Ana and her friend Kenji are having breakfast on a Saturday at a traditional café in the Gràcia neighborhood, in Barcelona.
Kenji orders a hot chocolate with whipped cream, and Jordi, the server, recommends the house coca to them, fresh out of the oven.
Ana looks at the coca and sees that the whole surface is covered in almonds.
Ana points to Kenji and explains to Jordi: He has a severe tree-nut allergy.
Jordi, with great kindness, offers to scrape the almonds off a slice for Kenji.
Ana: I really appreciate it, honestly, you're very kind.
Ana: Thanks, Jordi, but please don't scrape it.
Ana: I don't recommend Kenji try it, even if you remove the almonds.
Jordi admits that in the bakery kitchen they make the dough on the same table where they work with almonds all day.
Kenji hesitates and says that a small piece isn't going to hurt him.
Ana: Kenji, don't eat it; there are bits left in the dough.
Ana: Don't push it, Kenji; it's not worth the risk.
Kenji remembers that last year he had anaphylaxis from a piece of nougat.
He carries his antihistamine and his auto-injector, as his doctor told him, and Ana knows that, if there are symptoms, the auto-injector is used and 112 is called.
Ana: Do you have anything packaged, with the allergen label?
Jordi brings a packaged product, but the label says it may contain traces of tree nuts.
Ana: If there's no safe option, he'd rather not eat anything.

Jordi checks the allergen chart and confirms that the hot chocolate has no tree nuts among its ingredients; Ana asks whether it is prepared with clean utensils, and Kenji decides to order it only if the kitchen confirms.

sourceVerbsEnglish.meaningEnglish: to eat up, to eat (something whole)

lessons.objectiveFrenchCourseEnglish: Politely reject an offer to remove visible almonds for a friend with a serious tree-nut allergy.
lessons.focusEnglish: Use a warm refusal with merci, mais, then a clear negative request; ask about ingredients and cross-contact.
lessons.focusFrench: Refuser avec tact une option risquée et demander des informations vérifiables.
lessons.teachingNotesEnglish: Merci, mais introduces a polite refusal. The dialogue distinguishes removing visible nuts from questions about ingredients, shared dough and equipment. Ask the baker for current preparation details.

words.en: If the information is unclear, we will not order it.
words.fr: Si les informations ne sont pas claires, nous ne le commanderons pas.

english: Ana and Kenji enter a bakery in Paris and stop at the pastry counter.
Kenji has a serious tree-nut allergy and asks what is in a glazed pastry.
The baker says the pastry has almonds scattered over the top.
Ana thanks her for explaining and asks how the pastry is prepared.
The baker kindly offers to remove the visible almonds.
Ana answers: Thank you, but please do not just scrape them off.
She explains that pieces may remain in the dough or on shared equipment.
Kenji asks whether the baker has a current ingredient and allergen label.
The baker checks the label with them instead of guessing.
It lists tree nuts and a possible cross-contact warning.
Kenji says he will not order that pastry.
Ana replies: I appreciate your kindness; it is not worth the risk.
They ask whether a packaged product has clearer information.
Kenji remembers that he had anaphylaxis after eating nougat last year.
He carries his antihistamine and his epinephrine auto-injector, as his doctor instructed him.
Kenji decides not to order food from this counter; Ana knows the doctor’s instructions: if symptoms appear, use the auto-injector and call 112.
The baker cannot confirm the preparation details, so Kenji declines the drink too.
Ana thanks the baker again, and they continue to their planned alternative.
french: Ana et Kenji entrent dans une boulangerie à Paris et s’arrêtent au comptoir des pâtisseries.
Kenji a une allergie grave aux fruits à coque et demande ce que contient une pâtisserie glacée.
La boulangère dit que des amandes sont réparties sur la pâtisserie.
Ana la remercie pour l’explication et demande comment la pâtisserie est préparée.
La boulangère propose gentiment d’enlever les amandes visibles.
Ana répond : « Merci, mais n’enlevez pas simplement les amandes, s’il vous plaît. »
Elle explique que des morceaux peuvent rester dans la pâte ou sur du matériel partagé.
Kenji demande si la boulangère a une étiquette récente des ingrédients et des allergènes.
La boulangère vérifie l’étiquette avec eux au lieu de deviner.
Elle indique des fruits à coque et un avertissement sur un possible contact croisé.
Kenji dit qu’il ne commandera pas cette pâtisserie.
Ana répond : « Je vous remercie de votre gentillesse ; cela ne vaut pas le risque. »
Ils demandent si un produit emballé donne des informations plus claires.
Kenji se souvient qu’il a eu une anaphylaxie après avoir mangé du nougat l’année dernière.
Il a avec lui son antihistaminique et son auto-injecteur d’adrénaline, comme son médecin le lui a indiqué.
Kenji décide de ne pas commander de nourriture à ce comptoir ; Ana connaît les consignes du médecin : si des symptômes apparaissent, utiliser l’auto-injecteur et appeler le 112.
La boulangère ne peut pas confirmer les détails de préparation ; Kenji refuse donc aussi la boisson.
Ana remercie encore la boulangère, et ils poursuivent leur autre projet.

lessons.sourceTitleEnglish: Give Honest Feedback to a New Café Owner
lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Give specific, kind feedback on coffee and menu clarity and make two concrete recommendations.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: You are a customer, and the AI is Camila, the new café owner in Barrio Italia: give honest, kind feedback on the cortado and the chalkboard menu, and make two concrete recommendations using le recomiendo que and ojalá que with the present subjunctive.
lessons.sourceGrammarFocusEnglish: Present subjunctive after wishes and recommendations (le recomiendo que ponga los precios; ojalá que el café salga más caliente)

sourceWordsEnglish.en: If you want my honest opinion, the cortado arrived a bit cold.
I recommend that you warm the cups before serving.
I hope the cortado comes out a little hotter.
I suggest you separate the coffees from the sweets by category.
It's better if you write the prices in bigger letters.
I loved the kuchen, it was truly delicious.
I hope what I'm saying doesn't bother you.
I really hope things go great with the café, Camila.

sourcePassageEnglish: Daniel, a Canadian traveler, has a cortado and eats a raspberry kuchen at Camila's new café in Barrio Italia.
Camila opened the place two weeks ago and asks Daniel for his honest opinion about the coffee and the menu.
Daniel: If you want my honest opinion, the cortado arrived a bit cold.
Daniel: The crema looked very nice, but the steamed milk arrived lukewarm.
Camila explains that the espresso machine is new and that she is still learning to control the temperature.
She says that she adjusts the grinder every morning so that the espresso comes out well.
Daniel notices that the cup warmer is turned off on top of the machine.
Daniel: I recommend that you warm the cups before serving.
Daniel: I hope the cortado comes out a little hotter.
Then Daniel looks at the menu board, written in white chalk, and finds it confusing.
Daniel: The handwriting is very small and the prices are not readable from the register.
Daniel: I suggest you separate the coffees from the sweets by category.
Daniel: It's better if you write the prices in bigger letters.
Camila: You're right, the first impression is very important in a new place.
Daniel: I hope what I'm saying doesn't bother you.
Camila: Not at all, I really appreciate the suggestion.
Daniel: I loved the kuchen, it was truly delicious.
Daniel: I really hope things go great with the café, Camila.

sourceVerbsEnglish.exampleEnglish: I recommend that you warm the cups before serving.
I suggest you separate the coffees from the sweets by category.
Camila warms the cups before serving.
The cortado comes out lukewarm from the machine.
Camila writes the menu in white chalk.

sourceGrammarExamplesEnglish: I recommend that you put the prices next to each coffee.
I hope the milk comes out hotter tomorrow.
lessons.titleFrenchCourseEnglish: Donner un avis utile à une nouvelle propriétaire
lessons.objectiveFrenchCourseEnglish: Give kind, specific feedback about drink temperature and menu readability to a new Montréal café owner.
lessons.focusEnglish: Use je vous conseillerais de for a concrete suggestion and j’aimerais que for a desired change; balance criticism with a sincere compliment.
lessons.focusFrench: Exprimer un avis nuancé et formuler deux suggestions concrètes avec tact.
lessons.teachingNotesEnglish: A specific observation is more useful than a sweeping judgment: the drink arrived lukewarm, while the pastry was good. Suggest warming cups and making prices easier to read, then invite the owner’s view.

words.en: I wish you every success with the café.

passage.titleFrench: Donner un avis utile à une nouvelle propriétaire
english: Daniel visits a recently opened café in Montréal and orders coffee with a berry cake.
The owner, Camille, asks what he thinks of the drinks and the menu board.
Daniel says: If you want my honest opinion, the coffee arrived a little cool.
He adds that the espresso looked good but the steamed milk was lukewarm.
Camille says the machine is new and she is still learning its settings.
She shows him the grinder that the team adjusts every morning.
Daniel notices that the cup warmer is switched off.
He says: I would suggest warming the cups before serving.
Camille agrees to test it and ask customers whether the temperature improves.
Daniel then looks at the menu board written in white chalk.
From the register, he cannot read the small prices clearly.
He suggests separating the drinks from the pastries by category.
He adds: It would help to write the prices in larger letters.
Camille says the first impression matters for a new café.
Daniel asks whether his comments are useful or too direct.
Camille thanks him for being specific and kind.
Daniel says he loved the berry cake.
Before leaving, he wishes Camille success with the café.
french: Daniel entre dans un café récemment ouvert à Montréal et commande un café avec un gâteau aux petits fruits.
La propriétaire, Camille, lui demande ce qu’il pense des boissons et de l’ardoise.
Daniel dit : « Si vous voulez mon avis sincère, le café était un peu tiède. »
Il ajoute que l’expresso avait l’air bon, mais que le lait chauffé à la vapeur était tiède.
Camille dit que la machine est neuve et qu’elle apprend encore à la régler.
Elle lui montre le moulin que l’équipe règle chaque matin.
Daniel remarque que le chauffe-tasses est éteint.
Il dit : « Je vous conseillerais de réchauffer les tasses avant de servir. »
Camille accepte de faire un essai et de demander aux clients si la température s’améliore.
Daniel regarde ensuite l’ardoise écrite à la craie blanche.
Depuis la caisse, il n’arrive pas à lire clairement les petits prix.
Il suggère de séparer les boissons des pâtisseries par catégorie.
Il ajoute : « Ce serait plus clair d’écrire les prix en plus gros. »
Camille dit que la première impression compte pour un nouveau café.
Daniel demande si ses remarques sont utiles ou trop directes.
Camille le remercie d’avoir été précis et bienveillant.
Daniel dit qu’il a adoré le gâteau aux petits fruits.
Avant de partir, il souhaite à Camille beaucoup de succès avec son café.

verbs.exampleFrench: Je conseille de réchauffer les tasses.

verbs.exampleEnglish: I suggest separating drinks and pastries.
verbs.exampleFrench: Je suggère de séparer les boissons des pâtisseries.

verbs.exampleEnglish: Camille warms the cups before serving.
